project_overview.purpose: spring-rest-sakila is a Spring Boot 3 / Java 17 REST API service exposing the MySQL Sakila sample database (a DVD rental store: films, actors, customers, stores, rentals, payments). It is a sample/reference project demonstrating production-grade patterns for building a hypermedia-driven, secured CRUD API over a relational domain.
functionality: Full CRUD endpoints for the core Sakila domain: films, actors, customers, addresses/cities/countries, payments, rentals, staff, and stores (70 REST endpoints across 10 controllers)
Composite read models (e.g. film details, customer details, staff details) built from JPA projections and Querydsl queries
Reporting endpoints (sales by category, sales by store) under /reports
JWT-based stateless authentication via a /login endpoint, with role-based authorization (@Secured with ROLE_READ / ROLE_MANAGE) on every controller method
HATEOAS responses: every resource is wrapped in a representation model with self/related links via dedicated RepresentationModelAssemblers
Pagination, sorting, and filter options (e.g. film category/release-year/rating filters) on collection endpoints
Redis-backed caching configuration and Spring Actuator + Prometheus observability
API documentation generated from tests via Spring REST Docs, exported to OpenAPI 3 and Postman collections
project_overview.architecture: Layered architecture organized as a modular monolith: eight vertically sliced service packages (auth, catalog, customer, location, payment, rental, staff, store), each containing its own controller -> service -> repository -> domain (entity/dto/mapper/converter) stack, plus shared 'common' (base entities/DTOs, security, filters, exceptions, utilities) and 'config' (security, persistence, Redis, logging) packages. The slicing mirrors the author's companion microservices version, making each slice extractable. Controllers depend on service interfaces; implementations combine Spring Data JPA repositories with custom Querydsl repositories for complex queries; MapStruct mappers translate between entities and DTOs; HATEOAS assemblers shape the HTTP representation.
technology_stack: Spring Boot Web MVC - REST endpoints
Querydsl - type-safe custom queries and projections
Spring HATEOAS - hypermedia representation models and link building
Spring Security + JJWT - stateless JWT authentication and role-based authorization
Spring REST Docs + epages restdocs-api-spec - test-driven API docs, OpenAPI/Postman export
Spring Actuator + Prometheus - metrics and observability
Gradle (Kotlin DSL) with version catalogs; Kotlin kapt for annotation processing
design_patterns: Layered architecture with vertical (feature) slicing per bounded context
Repository pattern, extended with the custom-repository-fragment pattern (Custom*Repository + Impl) for Querydsl queries
DTO + Mapper (MapStruct) pattern separating persistence entities from API models
Assembler pattern (Spring HATEOAS RepresentationModelAssembler) for hypermedia output
Service interface / implementation separation enabling testability
Builder pattern (Lombok @Builder) for DTOs and filter options
Filter chain pattern for JWT authentication and request logging
Attribute Converter pattern (JPA @Converter) for enum-to-column mappings such as film rating and special features
noteworthy_aspects: Low overall complexity: average cyclomatic complexity 1.87 across 579 methods; 88% of methods are trivial (cc 1-4), consistent with thin controllers and delegation-heavy services

All 12 methods with cc > 10 are equals() implementations on large DTOs/entities (max cc 16 on Film/FilmEntity) - generated-style field-by-field comparisons, a maintenance smell that Lombok @EqualsAndHashCode could eliminate
Security is enforced uniformly: every controller handler carries @Secured, and JWT validation is implemented as a dedicated filter + AuthenticationProvider pair rather than ad-hoc checks
Strong consistency across the eight service slices (same package layout, naming, and assembler/mapper conventions) makes the codebase highly predictable and a good template for code generation
Heavy use of compile-time tooling (MapStruct, Querydsl APT, Lombok) shifts complexity out of runtime code but couples the build to annotation processing (kapt)
Documentation is test-driven (REST Docs), so API docs can only drift if tests fail - a notable best practice
No service-layer business invariants beyond CRUD orchestration: domain logic largely lives in the database model, which is typical for Sakila samples but limits the project as a DDD reference

class_summaries.com.example.app.App: Spring Boot application entry point; bootstraps the entire service.
class_summaries.com.example.app.services.auth.controller: Authentication endpoint: accepts user credentials at POST /login, delegates to the user-details and security services, and returns a signed JWT for use on subsequent requests.
class_summaries.com.example.app.services.auth.service.Jp: Spring Security UserDetailsService backed by the JPA user repository; loads user accounts and their roles for authentication.
class_summaries.com.example.app.services.auth.service.Se: Thin authentication facade that wraps a JWT and user details into a JwtAuthenticationToken and submits it to the AuthenticationManager.
class_summaries.com.example.app.common.security.JwtToken: Creates and validates signed JWTs (issuer, expiry, role claims) using the JJWT library; the cryptographic core of the auth subsystem.
class_summaries.com.example.app.common.security.JwtAuthe: Servlet filter that extracts the Bearer token from incoming requests and triggers token authentication before the request reaches controllers.
AuthenticationProvider that verifies JwtAuthenticationToken instances against the token provider, establishing the security context.
Spring Security Authentication implementation carrying the raw JWT plus principal and granted authorities.
class_summaries.com.example.app.config.SecurityFilterCon: Defines the SecurityFilterChain: stateless session policy, endpoint authorization rules, and registration of the JWT authentication filter.
class_summaries.com.example.app.config.AuthConfig: Authentication wiring: exposes the PasswordEncoder and AuthenticationManager beans used by login and the JWT provider.
class_summaries.com.example.app.config.PersistenceConfig: JPA/Querydsl configuration, including the shared JPAQueryFactory bean and auditing setup.
class_summaries.com.example.app.config.RedisConfig: Configures the Redis connection and cache manager used for response/entity caching.
class_summaries.com.example.app.config.LoggingFilterConf: Registers the request/response logging filter for HTTP traffic observability.
class_summaries.com.example.app.services.catalog.control: REST controller for /actors: paged actor listing, CRUD, and nested film resources for an actor, each secured by role and rendered through HATEOAS assemblers.

REST controller for /films: filtered/paged film listing (category, release year, rating), film CRUD, film details, rental price lookup, and nested actor sub-resources; read operations require ROLE_READ, mutations ROLE_MANAGE.
class_summaries.com.example.app.services.catalog.service: Catalog service orchestrating actor CRUD and actor-film queries across the JPA and custom Querydsl repositories, mapping entities to DTOs.
Catalog service implementing film CRUD, filtered listing, film-details projections, and rental price retrieval by combining standard and custom repositories with MapStruct mapping.
class_summaries.com.example.app.services.customer.contro: REST controller for /customers covering customer CRUD plus customer details, address, payment, and rental sub-resources.
class_summaries.com.example.app.services.customer.servic: Service layer for customer management; coordinates customer repositories and mappers and exposes composite customer-details views.
class_summaries.com.example.app.services.location.contro: REST controller for location resources (addresses, cities, countries) with paged listing and lookups.
class_summaries.com.example.app.services.location.servic: Service aggregating address/city/country repositories to serve location queries and composite address details.
class_summaries.com.example.app.services.payment.control: REST controller for /payments: paged payment listing, lookup, creation and deletion.
class_summaries.com.example.app.services.payment.service: Service handling payment CRUD and customer/staff payment queries via JPA and Querydsl repositories.
class_summaries.com.example.app.services.rental.controll: REST controller for /rentals supporting rental listing, lookup, creation (rent) and update (return) flows.
Service implementing the rental lifecycle - creating rentals, recording returns, and querying rental history.
class_summaries.com.example.app.services.staff.controlle: REST controller for /staffs exposing staff CRUD and staff-details composite views.
class_summaries.com.example.app.services.staff.service.S: Service layer for staff management combining staff repositories, custom queries, and DTO mapping.
class_summaries.com.example.app.services.store.controlle: REST controller for /stores: store listing, lookup, CRUD, and nested staff/details sub-resources.
Read-only reporting controller under /reports exposing sales-by-category and sales-by-store aggregations.
class_summaries.com.example.app.services.store.service.S: Service orchestrating store CRUD and store-details queries.
class_summaries.com.example.app.services.store.service.R: Service computing sales aggregation reports through custom Querydsl repository queries.
class_summaries.com.example.app.common.exception.GlobalE: Centralized @RestControllerAdvice translating application exceptions into consistent HTTP error responses.

services.auth: Authentication is cleanly separated: controller handles HTTP, JpaUserDetailsService handles lookup, SecurityService handles token authentication, and JWT mechanics live in common.security.
Role model is coarse (READ/MANAGE), applied declaratively via @Secured constants.
services.catalog: Largest slice (62 types): films and actors with nested sub-resources, attribute converters for rating/special-features enums, and Querydsl projections for film details.
DTO equals() methods here are the project's top complexity hotspots (cc up to 16).
services.customer: Composite CustomerDetails projection joins customer, address, and activity data through a custom repository.
services.location: Address/city/country hierarchy with converters for country/language enums; serves as the shared location backbone for customer, staff, and store slices.
services.payment: Straightforward CRUD slice; queries support filtering payments by customer and staff.
services.rental: Encodes the rent/return lifecycle; uses a value-object package (vo) for rental status concepts.
services.staff: Mirrors the customer slice structure with staff-details composite views.
services.store: Hosts both store resource endpoints and the cross-cutting sales ReportController.
common: Shared kernel: base entity/DTO types with auditing, JWT security components, logging filter, global exception handling, and serializers - reused by every slice.
config: All framework wiring (security chain, persistence/Querydsl, Redis cache, logging) is isolated here, keeping slices framework-light.

method_descriptions.com.example.app.services.catalog.control: Returns a paged, HATEOAS-wrapped list of films, optionally filtered by category, release year, and rating (ROLE_READ).
Creates a new film from the request body and responds 201 with a Location header pointing at the created resource (ROLE_MANAGE).
Fetches a single film by id, returning 404 when absent (ROLE_READ).
Updates an existing film with the supplied request payload (ROLE_MANAGE).
Deletes the film identified by filmId (ROLE_MANAGE).
method_descriptions.com.example.app.services.auth.service.Se: Wraps the JWT and user identity into a JwtAuthenticationToken and authenticates it via the AuthenticationManager.
method_descriptions.com.example.app.config.AuthConfig#passwo: Exposes the PasswordEncoder bean used to hash and verify user credentials.
method_descriptions.com.example.app.config.AuthConfig#authen: Builds the AuthenticationManager bean that backs login and JWT verification.
